messages:
maria (devex): quick heads-up — the Go sample app for generator streaming is hanging when we cancel the parent context after an auth refresh.

maria (devex): repro is pretty small: start a generator stream, let the auth hook refresh token mid-stream, then call cancel(). the recv goroutine doesn't exit.

maria (devex): snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() {
  for {
    token, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { break }
    // process token
  }
}()
// auth refresh happens async, then we call cancel() below
// cancel() returns, but goroutine still running
```

kai (go-sdk): ugh. thanks for the report. I think this is a mix of two things: (1) our internal retry/backoff loop holding on to the original ctx inside an auth refresh path, and (2) Recv() blocking on an internal channel without checking ctx.Done().

kai (go-sdk): quick question — is this happening only when the auth token rotates (i.e. we re-run auth provider and re-initialize transport)? or also on transient network retries?

maria (devex): seen it mainly with token rotation from our local dev auth hook. but sam saw something similar on flaky network where Cancel didn't unstick a long-running stream. so probably both.

oliver (runtime): we wrap the transport in a retry loop that does exponential backoff. currently that loop takes a context but we also spawn a goroutine for token refresh which passes a child ctx. possible we leak the stream's recv loop if the transport layer switches underneath.

sam (sre): can reproduce in CI with a tiny harness where we force token TTL to 1s and then cancel after 2s — recv still running and allocs go up.

maria (devex): proposal for DX/API change: either add RecvContext(ctx) to the stream API or make GeneratorStream return a pair (stream, cancelFunc) where stream.Recv respects the original ctx as well as an explicit Close() method.

kai (go-sdk): I prefer Recv(ctx) so caller can control per-Recv timeouts and cancelation. Something like:
```go
token, err := stream.Recv(ctx)
```
That keeps current ergonomics but makes cancelation explicit. We should keep the existing Recv() as sugar but implement it as Recv(context.Background()) to avoid breaking.

oliver (runtime): on runtime side we should also ensure auth refresh uses a separate ctx and doesn't keep references to the stream's ctx after swap. I'll audit the transport swap logic.

maria (devex): small patch idea: before swapping transports, signal a drain channel to the recv loop and wait up to 200ms for it to exit; if it doesn't, log a debug and force-close the stream. This avoids orphaned goroutines in dev/local flows.

kai (go-sdk): sounds reasonable. I'll file a small API PR: add RecvWithContext(ctx) and make Recv() forward to it. Also fix auth refresh path to cancel any internal per-stream child contexts on transport swap.

sam (sre): adding a test harness would be great. I can add a flaky-transport test that simulates token rotation + cancel and fails the build until fixed.

ci-bot: build triggered: go-sdk/generator:pr-3224 — tests: flaky-transport-cancel will run.

maria (devex): awesome — thanks. last ask: can we document the pattern in the sample app (recommended cancellation pattern) so new users don't run into this? a 1-paragraph note in the generator README should help onboarding.

kai (go-sdk): yup will add doc blurb and a short code example using context timeouts. assigning to me and oliver for runtime followup.

maria (devex): thanks everyone :thumbsup:
